SourceBodyRead retains data and an optional exact EOF/failure category together. Native known-length H1 reads pair their last data with EOF while holding the body lock; expectation EOF is set from that read result. H2 keeps its subsequent-read EOF behavior. Empty successful reads are not EOF.

ReadAll retains its initial Reader, starts at 512 logical source bytes, applies source byte-slice nextslicecap/noscan size-class growth and consumes returned bytes before an error. Its low-level result retains partial bytes on failure. Form parsing wraps the retained Reader with a 10MiB+1 limit, preserving ReadAll error precedence before size rejection.

SourceJsonDecoder is shared by webhook and gateway consumers: retain the Reader, compact only on refill, grow logical capacity by 2*cap+512, scan data before its paired read error, and discard that local error if a value completes. Sticky framing/read failures and successful semantic decoding remain separate.

Gateway dispatch captures current URL.Path before its ParseForm/body reader call, as in source. Form query parsing reads current URL.RawQuery after the body read and permits nil URL. Gateway component/parameter/form text representations, form caches/partial states and parameter-limit binding remain explicit unfinished work.

SourceValues reuses the existing shared byte-key map/string-slice backing with exact case-sensitive append, nil versus empty maps/slices, indexed aliases, source allocation capacity and existing JSON byte-string serialization. GatewayCall.form now retains that map rather than a lossy BTreeMap<String,Vec<String>>.

RequestFields owns nil-initialized Form and PostForm; getters/assignment retain map identities. The fixed gateway fallback preserves ParseForm cache order: parse PostForm even when Form is already set, allocate an empty PostForm after failed/absent body parsing, copy body values first, merge current URL query second, and skip already initialized caches on later calls.

URL query parsing returns a non-nil map and optional error together. It continues past bad names/values, preserves all valid pairs, appends duplicate values in input order, keeps the first escape error, and lets each later semicolon error overwrite the prior error as in the source. QueryUnescape retains arbitrary bytes and plus-to-space behavior; typed invalid escapes retain the original at-most-three-byte segment.

The fixed gateway form path retains nil-Body missing-form error, ReadAll bytes/error handling, 10MiB+1 body bound and POST-too-large result. It assigns partial PostForm values on query errors, still populates Form from the current optional URL after body errors, and preserves the body error over the later query error. Cached errors are not replayed once the source maps are initialized.

SourceQueryProfile explicitly supplies source allocation/word size and selected urlmaxqueryparams bytes. Both selected Go sources default to at most 10000 ampersand-counted parameters; valid custom values use zero=unlimited or params<custom, invalid/source-int-overflow values fall back to default, negative values retain their source comparison, and a differing default/custom decision increments the shared nondefault counter. The source second setting read before Atoi is retained.

UtilityRuntimeProviders statically delegates SourceQuerySettingsGetter through UseField(source_query_settings); UtilityRuntimeOwner constructs one explicit Go126/64 default data profile. No Rust-host fallback, environment probe, automatic GODEBUG binding, native metric publication or completed source-profile credit is inferred.

Gateway dispatch splits the captured URL.Path into Bytes without UTF8-lossy conversion. Pattern literals, verbs, wildcard/multi/concat stacks, capture names and values retain bytes through the actual raw callback; duplicate capture keys overwrite in source variable order in a HashMap<Bytes,Bytes>.

GatewayPattern.new retains the supplied HeaderValues []string slice backing and its view length/capacity. Literal operations and source string rendering read the live pool. NewPattern copies variable name values when processing capture operations, so later pool edits do not rename captures. Registered pattern copies retain that same literal backing.

Byte suffix splitting preserves exact colon/verb bytes, including a verb containing a colon, empty-prefix 404 handling on same-method routes and the separate other-method fallback path. GatewayPattern.string_bytes is the canonical Pattern.String operation; fmt::Display is only a lossy text compatibility view.

SourceUppercaseMapper is statically delegated through UtilityRuntimeProviders and reads the SourceUnicodeProfile getter. Header override bytes captured before ParseForm are mapped afterward through the same runtime context. Go single-rune uppercase and per-invalid-byte UTF8 replacement replace the prior Rust expanding/lossy conversion.

Tracked original Go1.26.5 Unicode15 and Go1.27.1 Unicode17 tables.go artifacts supply immutable data. The Rust reader projects only numeric CaseRanges uppercase deltas into disposable OnceLock lookup caches, then uses source binary-range lookup and UpperLower even-offset conversion. No production Go body is parsed/evaluated and no Rust source is generated from Go text.

The default runtime context explicitly selects Go1265. Both source Unicode profiles are authored, but actual application/compiler/profile binding, source string/builder identity/capacity/allocation/panic behavior and native integration remain unverified required work.

GatewayPattern.new now accepts i64 version/opcode operands with an explicit Go32/Go64 PatternWordProfile. Ingress values and stack/tail arithmetic use source-word normalization/wrapping. All constructor rejection branches carry their exact selected numeric value/message through the existing CGP runtime.

PatternConstruction retains a zero GatewayPattern plus an optional shared-identity invalid-pattern error on rejection, and the real pattern plus nil error on success. into_result is an explicit Rust projection. InvalidPatternError copies retain one private static identity token; direct equality helper is distinct from wrapped-error traversal.

Constructor diagnostics distinguish unsupported version, odd opcode count, duplicate pushM, literal/concat/capture indices, stack underflow and invalid opcode with the source messages, including source misleading negative-literal wording for positive out-of-bounds indices.

SourcePatternLogger models the default Error/Fatal stderr profile plus explicit discard/JSON choices. It checks discard before formatting user Error values, uses source severity prefixes/local standard-log date-time or sorted JSON message/severity fields, appends only a missing newline and ignores the single Write result. General formatter/caller/native writer/global configuration profiles remain open.

MustPattern is consumed by SourceGatewayPatternConstructor.require_source_gateway_pattern: nil error returns the given pattern; nonnil error emits the fatal initialization message and invokes the existing CGP SourceProcessExit(1). An unexpectedly returning exit provider panics instead of reporting success. No fatal path was executed.

GatewayContext new_pattern/must_pattern/handle_compiled provide a connected compiled-registration path through RuntimeProviders and the existing route table. Actual generated SDK/allocator initializer and command adoption remains M0025/M0027, without registration-only acceptance credit.

GatewayPattern retains its explicit PatternWordProfile through successful/rejected construction, zero(profile), cloning and registered routes. max_int is source i32::MAX/i64::MAX, independent of the Rust host.

Source strings.Join slash helper preserves empty/single-element fast paths, including immutable single-string reuse, the source strict separator >= maxInt/(count-1) guard and ordered element remaining-length checks.

Source concat helper skips empty parts, reuses a sole nonempty immutable string and checks the selected source integer bound before concatenating. Matcher verb fallback and the no-verb Pattern.String slash prefix consume it.

Pattern.String capture braces and nonempty-verb rendering follow their two fixed byte-only Sprintf forms, with per-append source-int overflow classification kept distinct from runtime concatenation. This is not a general Go formatter or a complete printer-pool/heap/allocator profile.

SourcePatternStringCompletion routes Join overflow to a string panic, fixed-format overflow to a typed recoverable runtime-error projection, and concat overflow to stderr fatal prefix plus SourceProcessExit(2). A returning exit provider aborts; runtime.throw is not downgraded to recoverable panic or pattern-logger output.

GatewayDispatcher passes its runtime capability for both same-method and other-method matching. Canonical Pattern.string_bytes consumes the same provider; try_string_bytes returns an explicit Rust result and Display returns fmt::Error on a length failure rather than claiming source effect equivalence.

Matcher borrows the input components on equal verbs and rejects a nonempty mismatching pattern verb before copying. It copies only when source verb fallback must change the last component; empty fallback creates one component.
